manifest.name: dsh-engram
manifest.description: Minimalist long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness, distilling symbolic-index + pi-esr ideas: zero-LLM auto-capture, a symbolic [ENGRAM] index with progressive disclosure, and an ESR-lite evidence-closure protocol (esr_task / esr_node / esr_close / esr_link). Real agent-behaviour telemetry (usage rollup + /stats) and a deterministic offline recall benchmark (npm run eval). Hot path is model-free; storage on ctx.storageDomain; web memory viewer, observability panel and config card through DSH's native settings slots.

bundle.text:
# dsh-engram bundle patch: inserts the host plugin row into the web profile
# roster. Activate with:
#   dsh plugin --profile web add file:/Users/sunchuxiong/dsh-loom
#
# The row is a bare host-half plugin by package name. It does not need to
# enable storage-domain / storage-json / session-query-sqlite — the standard
# web profile (dsh-base x dsh-web-app) already mounts them.

# dsh-engram REPLACES the host-plane auto-compact: its Context GC engine
# provides the `compaction` service (see docs/PROPOSAL-contextgc.zh.md).
# cordis refuses two sibling rows registering the same service key, so the
# base row must be disabled here — this patch layer wins because bundle patch
# layers apply in bundle order and dsh-engram loads after dsh-base. Removing
# dsh-engram from the profile re-arms the base row automatically.
# NOTE: with `gcReplacesCompaction:false`, dsh-engram still mounts a plain
# BasicCompactionEngine, so compaction never goes away while it is installed.
# The host-plane provider is mounted by `lib/index.js` (`mountCompactionEngine`);
# the WEB plane is auto-wired at boot when `autoWebCompaction` is on (opt-in
# since v0.6, default off): the plugin swaps the `compaction-basic` row for
# `dsh-engram/compaction` in every stock-layout preset — default + full roster
# (shipped `agent.cordis.yml` roots and DSH ≥ 0.2.0 declarative
# `dsh-web-app/presets/*.patch.yml`; idempotent, backed up, never touches a
# custom or no-compaction preset; manual CLI
# `npm run web-compaction:status|enable|revert`).
- id: compaction-basic
  disabled: true

# BoundaryPrune (ResultPack L1) needs DSH's `toolResultPruner` service on the
# HOST plane. DSH ≥ 0.2.0 web profiles move compaction + the pruner into each
# agent preset's isolate realm and disable the host-plane `tool-result-pruner`
# row, so the host plugin's L1 found no service and silently went dormant (the
# Context Ledger then never credited pruning savings). Re-arm the host row here
# — the preset realm keeps its own copy for compaction-time pruning, so both
# paths coexist. Without this, `boundaryPrune` only works on headless/TUI/base
# profiles. Verify via the status snapshot's `boundaryPrune.armed`.
- id: tool-result-pruner
  disabled: false

- insert:
    - id: engram
      name: dsh-engram

readme.text:
> **[English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh.md)**

[](https://github.com/skepsun/dsh-engram/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Minimalist long-term memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), distilled from the
[symbolic-index](https://github.com/skepsun/symbolic-index) and [pi-esr](https://github.com/skepsun/pi-esr) ideas —
with one goal: **save tokens**.

- **Zero-LLM intake** — auto-captures meaningful events from tool results by pure
  pattern matching (git milestones with a written `-m` commit message, edits to
  key files, repeated errors), plus an explicit `engram_store`. Nothing on the hot
  path calls a model, and pure plumbing — `git push` / `git stash` / silent
  commits — is deliberately never recorded (see *Auto-capture policy* below).
  Every write is run through a deterministic **secret redactor** first — API
  keys, JWTs, `Bearer` tokens, private keys, AWS/Stripe/Slack/GitHub tokens and
  `key=value` secret shapes are replaced with `<REDACTED:…>` markers before the
  dedup hash, the char cap, and storage, so sensitive text can never land on
  disk. Failing **test runs** are recognized by pure patterns (`npm test`,
  `node --test`, vitest/pytest/jest, failure lines) and captured as
  `tags:["error","test"]` entries with a raised signal. DSH **goal-domain
  integration**: a completed or blocked goal (`goal/change` session event)
  auto-sediments as a `handoff`/`error` memory (`tag:goal`), so the outcome of
  a goal survives its session (see the `GET /api/dsh-engram/goals` read surface).
- **User-correction / preference l

```
MIT   ·   node >= 22.19   ·   host-half + browser-half in one package
```

Surveys of the existing DSH plugin ecosystem show the recall-bridge, approval-gate,
LLM-distillation and vector/graph niches are already crowded. dsh-engram fills the
three gaps that matter for token discipline:

1. **No model in the write path** — capture is deterministic pattern matching.
2. **No raw text in the prompt** — a bounded symbolic index is injected, plus the
   top ≤ N memories auto-recalled for the session's first message (within budget);
   deeper retrieval stays on demand ("retrieved ≠ full-text injected").
3. **Honest task closure** — STABLE cannot be declared without evidence.

DSH already provides cross-session FTS (`ctx.sessionQuery`), storage
(`ctx.storageDomain`), prompt-injection hooks and settings slots; dsh-engram is a
thin composition layer over them, not a re-implementation.

The DSH plugin ecosystem is young and unvetted — there is no official directory,
no signature check, and the harness's read/write permission tiers do **not**
constrain what a plugin's own code can do. So the trust bar for a memory plugin
is higher than for a tool: a memory plugin sits on your prompt prefix and writes
to disk on your behalf. dsh-engram's model, stated plainly:

- **No network, ever.** The plugin has no outbound socket, no telemetry, no
  update pinger. Nothing here can leak your sessions off the machine.
- **No shell, no filesystem access beyond one storage file.** It never executes
  commands and never touches arbitrary paths. All data lives in the single
  storage-domain unit `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_engram.json` (plus the session-log
  reads it makes through DSH's own `ctx.sessionQuery`).
- **Secrets are redacted before they can land on disk.** Every write path —
  `engram_store`, auto-capture, and the import/restore route — runs text through
  the deterministic `redactText` rule engine (API keys, JWTs, `Bearer` tokens,
  private keys, `key=value` secret shapes) *before* the dedup hash, the char
  cap, and storage. Nothing sensitive is ever persisted, so nothing sensitive
  can be recalled later.
- **Doing harm requires your harness's own permissions.** The plugin only *asks*
  the host to do things via the same seams the tools you already trust use. It
  does not widen sandbox policy or escalate to `danger-full-access` — if you
  keep your profile's defaults, engram inherits exactly those bounds.
- **Read-mostly web API, loopback-fenced.*

What this deliberately does **not** claim: it is not an air-gap. If your profile
grants the agent `danger-full-access` or a shell, the agent can use those —
engram is a memory layer, not a sandbox. The point above is that *dsh-engram
itself* adds no surface of its own.

Memory should not be a hostage. The four tables (memories / tasks / links /
entities) can be dumped and restored through a stable, versioned, machine-readable
shape — so the corpus survives a reinstall, a machine move, or (when a thin
adapter is written) a move to another harness, MCP end-point or Claude Code
skill. The contract is plain JSON with a self-describing header:

```http
GET  /api/dsh-engram/export?workspace=/path/to/project   # one workspace
GET  /api/dsh-engram/export                              # every workspace
```

```jsonc
{
  "meta": { "format": "dsh-engram/export", "version": 1, "exportedAt": 1724…, "workspace": "/path/to/project" },
  "memories": [ /* all rows, archived included — a backup never loses provenance */ ],
  "tasks":    [ /* draft/active/stable + archived */ ],

Restore is idempotent by default and gated when destructive:

- **`mode: "merge"`** (default) — writes only rows whose `id` is absent, so a
  backup can be re-applied any number of times without duplicating anything. Each
  row keeps its own `workspace`.
- **`mode: "replace"`** — wipes the target `workspace` from all four tables, then
  restores only its rows. Destructive, so it additionally requires
  `confirm: "restore"` in the body.
- **`dryRun: true`** — computes the identical plan (what would be written /
  skipped) without writing a single row.
- **Import honors the same invariants as `storeMemory`**: memory text passes the
  secret redactor before touching disk, and rows that would break the contract
  (missing id/workspace, empty text, over `maxMemoryChars`, id already present
  in merge, over the workspace memory cap) are skipped and listed in the
  response report instead of aborting the batch.

A restore round-trip for one workspace is then:

```sh
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-engram/export?workspace=$PWD" -o engram-backup.json
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-engram/import \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"payload\": $(cat engram-backup.json), \"mode\": \"merge\"}"

- **DSH 版本 / DSH versions**: `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` (本版 `0.9.0`; 已发布的 `0.3.7`、`0.4.0` 仍声明旧的 `0.1.x` 范围 `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.2.0-0` — 见下方矩阵)
- **最后验证日期 / Last verified**: 2026-10-27 — DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (`dsh --version`), web profile live composition; npm test 483/483
- **安装方式已验证 / Verified install**: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-engram`

> **Short version.** Every **published** release (`0.2.0` … `0.3.6`) supports
> the **old** DSH API graph (`0.1.0-rc.7` / `0.1.1`, peers `^0.1.0-rc.7`)
> **only**. DSH `0.1.2-alpha.2` and newer are **not** compatible with those
> releases — the settings/client API family broke there. New-DSH support
> **starts with `0.3.7`**, the first release of the new API generation
> (described below).

`0.1.2-alpha.2` is the first version of the new API family and the first that
**breaks** the released plugin versions:

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` **removed** `settingsNamespace()` and
  `installSettingsSection()` — the exact imports every release ≤ `0.3.6` uses —
  and replaced them with `settings.installSection`. The old host half fails to
  load on `0.1.2-alpha.2+`.
- The web client half swapped its inject set: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime`
  no longer exists in the new family (replaced by `dsh-api-remotes` plus
  `dsh-client-locale` / `-conversation` / `-renderer` / `-ui-settings-plugins`),
  and the settings card used to talk through `ctx.remote.settings`.
- Supporting bumps at the same boundary: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1 → ^4.0.2`,
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `^3.18.1 → ^3.18.2`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh` stopped
  shipping `config/agent-presets` in the package (moved to `dsh.configTrees`).

The web config card no longer depends on any of this: since `0.3.7` it reads
and writes the `dsh-engram` settings namespace through the plugin's **own**
HTTP route (`/api/dsh-engram/settings`, same-origin fetch like the memory
viewer), so the card is generation-agnostic on both sides of the
`0.1.2-alpha.2` boundary.

**One more settings break, at `0.1.7` / `0.2.0`** — and the reason `0.4.0` was
not actually loadable on the current DSH: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` **removed
`settings.installSection` again** in `0.1.7-alpha.2` (and keeps it removed in
`0.2.x`). The new settings model is **entry-keyed**: editable fields are
`.volatile()` fields of the plugin's own `Config` (validated + hot-committed by
the loader), and the settings form is keyed by the profile entry id (`engram`),
so nothing needs "mounting". `0.5.0` feature-detects the two generations in
`installEngramSettings`:

- DSH `≥0.1.7` / `0.2.x` — the 34 GUI knobs are the volatile `Config` fields
  (`lib/settings.js` `makeEngineConfigSchema`, exported as `Config` from
  `lib/index.js`); the card reads/writes entry `engram` through the same
  `/api/dsh-engram/settings` HTTP route, and the `service.settings` seam
  re-syncs `resolved` on `loader/volatile-update` so card edits land live on
  new sessions.
- DSH `≤0.1.5` — the legacy `settings.installSection` namespace (`dsh-engram`)
  is registered as before; nothing changes.

The declared range `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` covers both, and the HTTP wire
namespace stays `dsh-engram` on both generations (the seam's active namespace
drives mutations).

So: keep DSH on `0.1.1-rc.2` or older while running a release ≤ `0.3.6`, and
upgrade the plugin to `>=0.3.7` before moving DSH to `0.1.2-alpha.2`.

**L1 boundary prune was silently dormant on some profiles** — a boot-ordering
race, not a missing patch.

`BoundaryPrune` resolved DSH's `toolResultPruner` with a strict
`ctx.get("toolResultPruner")` at install time. On DSH `0.2.0` web profiles the
pruner's fiber activates **~100 ms after** the plugin (measured on the live
composition `dsh-context` + `dshmarket` + `dsh-engram`: `t0 strict=undefined /
loose=object`, strict resolves 100 ms later), so the strict lookup was empty,
`installBoundaryPrune` gave up, and L1 never armed for the life of the process —
taking the ledger's only prune-credit leg with it. The status snapshot also
reported that race as "row missing", pointing at the wrong fix.

- **Arm through `ctx.inject(["toolResultPruner"], …)`** — cordis runs the
  callback the moment the service becomes active (and again after a reload), so
  arming no longer depends on composition order; the durable status snapshot is
  rewritten as soon as L1 is armed.
- **"Absent" and "late" now read differently** — `boundaryPruneAvailability`
  falls back to a non-strict lookup: a disabled/missing row still says
  `no toolResultPruner service … (the bundle patch must re-enable …)`, a
  registered-but-inactive one says `registered but its fiber is not active yet`.
- **Verified** — the live bundle composition (with `dsh-context`) reproduces
  `armed:false` in an isolated `DSH_HOME`; after the fix the same composition
  reports `armed:true · threshold 8192`. `npm test` 406/406.

Web-plane Context GC on DSH `0.2.0`'s **declarative presets** — the preset
format changed shape (one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration inside
`dsh-web-app/presets/*.patch.yml`), and the auto-wiring was anchored to the old
`agent.cordis.yml` layout, so `autoWebCompaction` silently skipped every preset
(and could half-rewrite a stock row: the pattern did not include its trailing
newline).

- **Structural row location** — the `compaction` group is found by YAML
  structure (a list item carrying `group: true`), not by column position; the
  stock/engram rows are validated by BOTH their `- id:` and `name:` values, and
  the replacement inherits the row's own indent. Legacy `agent.cordis.yml`
  (4 spaces) and declarative patch files (14/16/18 spaces) both round-trip
  byte-identically.
- **Declarative discovery** — the preset roster no longer carries `path` on
  DSH `0.2.0`; the plugin maps each roster id to the shipped
  `<presetsDir>/<id>.patch.yml` (resolved through the `dsh` install, with
  `DSH_WEB_PRESETS_DIR` override) and skips user-defined declarative presets
  (profile-patch overrides) with an explicit log line instead of failing.
- **Status/doctor** — `npx dsh-engram status`/`doctor` discover both preset
  generations, show the detected layout, and flag `autoWebCompaction=false`
  (the opt-in toggle that makes the web plane a no-op), node_modules preset
  wiring (survives `npm update dsh` only while auto-wiring stays on), and
  profile-patch `preset-*` overrides that outrank the shipped files.
- **Migration** — restart `dsh web` with `autoWebCompaction:true`:

From event records to **maintainable current truth**: sessions sediment an
episode at teardown, new sessions get a resume brief, `esr_node` becomes a
readable page, and file anchors make stale truth detectable.

- **Session episode** — zero-LLM digest at `session/disposed` (files / commands /
  failures→fixed / decisions / open loops), never indexed, newest 20 per
  workspace kept.
- **Resume brief** — the newest episode from the last 7 days is injected as a
  `[RESUME]` line (≤240 chars + drill pointer) at session start.
- **Entity pages + cards** — `truth / timeline / open loops / conflicts /
  relations`; up to 2 one-line cards in the index, full page via
  `engram_detail(entity=…)`.
- **Revalidatable anchors** — file-backed memories record `mtime/size/sha256`;
  a bounded revalidation at session start tags changed/missing sources `stale`
  (dropped from index/truth, still re-fetchable).
- **Layered TTL** — preference/procedure permanent, episode 14d, error 60d,
  others 180d.
- **Migration** — only new writes are anchored (no historical backfill);
  restart `dsh web` after upgrading; an episode appears after one session ends,
  the resume brief on the next new session. The `0.6.0` ledger / defaults / JIT
  behaviour is unchanged.

The published `0.4.0` declared `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.2.0-0` — which the semver
gate **rejects on every DSH `0.2.0-0` prerelease** (`<0.2.0-0` excludes
`0.2.0-rc.x`), and its host settings half still called the `installSection`
API that `dsh-settings 0.1.7+` removed. `0.5.0` fixes **both**: the range
opens to `<0.3.0-0` (verified against DSH's own `includePrerelease` check, so
`0.2.0-rc.2` and the whole `0.2.x` line pass), and the settings card is
migrated onto the entry-id **volatile Config** model described above (with a
feature-detected legacy fallback).

| Component | Supported range |
| --- | --- |
| DSH runtime / host / client package family | `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `^4.0.2` |
| `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `^3.18.2` |
| Node.js | `>=22.19.0` |

`0.1.2-alpha.2` is the minimum version for this API family: host settings are
**feature-detected** — on DSH `≤0.1.5` they register the `dsh-engram`
namespace via `settings.installSection`; on `≥0.1.7` / `0.2.x` the form is the
plugin's `Config` with the 34 GUI knobs marked `.volatile()` (entry id
`engram`). The browser settings card reads and writes through the plugin's own
HTTP route (`/api/dsh-engram/settings`, see Route B above) on both. The full
regression suite (npm test 396/396, incl. the new settings-v2 coverage for the
volatile-Config model) passes against the DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` dependency set
(cordis 4.0.4 + schemastery 3.18.4 + cosmokit, matching the global DSH CLI).
The `.volatile()`/loader hot-commit path and the describe-side projection were
verified against the real `dsh-settings 0.2.0-rc.2` utilities, and a full
real-machine boot smoke on an isolated `dsh 0.2.0-rc.2` profile **passed**:
the plugin boots with no version-range denial, the settings card form is
served for entry `engram` (all 27 GUI knobs, incl. `trustedHosts`), and a
GET → PUT (`mutate` ops, revision 0→1) → unset round trip on
`/api/dsh-engram/settings` lands in the profile row and reads back. The older
`

To install the DSH version used for validation:

```sh
npm install --global @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2
dsh --version
```
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:skepsun/dsh-engram
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-engram

dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-engram
```

Then **restart `dsh web`**. Data persists in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_engram.json`.

> The npm and GitHub installs below need **no manual dependency step**: pnpm
> installs `zod` and vendors the optional `@deepseek-ai/*` peers into the
> plugin's own `node_modules`, and the CLI auto-registers the plugin into the
> profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`. The `setup-links` step below is only for
> the `link:` development workflow, where pnpm deliberately does not install a
> symlinked directory's dependencies.

> A fresh session is required to see the injected `[ENGRAM]`/`[ESR]` blocks and the
> tools; both prompts and the tools registry are assembled per session.

A *symlinked* plugin resolves its imports from its own `node_modules`, so the
host-side dependencies must be present **next to the checkout** — they are not
tracked by git:

```sh
cd /path/to/dsh-engram
node scripts/setup-links.mjs     # one command: links the @deepseek-ai
                                 # workspace packages into node_modules AND
                                 # installs zod (reused from the harness

The script auto-locates the harness checkout at `../deepseek-harness` (also
works when it sits next to the repo's *parent*, e.g. `E:\deepseek-harness` +
`E:\kototoro_demo\dsh-engram`); override with `DSH_HARNESS_DIR`. Without this
step, `dsh web` boot fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package
'zod'` (and would fail on the `@deepseek-ai/*` peers next). `node
scripts/setup-links.mjs --check` prints the state without writing anything.

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
- **Sidebar "ESR 看板" entry + full-screen kanban** — one more row under
  New Session with a **live active-task badge** (polled from /overview every
  30s across all workspaces). Clicking it opens a full-screen board in the
  center column: **草稿 / 进行中(gaps) / 就绪(evidence ready) / 已闭环** columns,
  workspace filter + search, an inline create form, and per-card
  "补齐证据 → 关闭" closure forms sharing the esr_close gates (artifact +
  evaluation + memory_refs). A **看板 / 图谱 (board/graph)** toggle in the
  header reuses the full relation graph (esr_node/esr_link force-directed SVG:
  entity circles + task check badges, drag/zoom/select for relation details),
  following the workspace filter and refreshed by the same 20s polling.
  Following the task-board precedent, the entry and
  the board are DOM-mounted and self-heal (MutationObserver re-inserts on shell
  re-renders), with cross-panel exclusivity against task-board/ssh (opening one
  evicts the others; clicking a sidebar session/workspace row hands the center
  column back to the conversation). The conversation subtree stays mounted
  underneath and is hidden by `html[data-dsh-engram-board-active]`, so toggling loses
  no state.

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
- **Unified task strip above the composer** — the conversation dock that DSH
  ships for its built-in todo tool is taken over (same `conversation.input.dock`
  cell / `id: todo` at a lower priority) and **merged** into one modern control:
  the session's current plan (`todo_write`'s `todos` projection) plus the
  workspace's persistent **ESR tasks** (with evidence-gap badges and an inline
  "补齐证据 → close" form) plus the **relation graph** rendered as
  node → relation → node chips with entity/task names resolved. It only shows
  while there is something to show, stays live with 15s polling, and the built-in
  plan still renders (without the ESR parts) if the loopback-fenced API is
  unreachable. A **workspace-switcher chip** leads the strip: it defaults to
  following the current session (the tooltip says so), and its dropdown pins the
  ESR task/relation source to any workspace (✓ marks the active pin; the × or
  "follow session" entry reverts). Switching refetches immediately and is a pure
  UI focus change — the model's session context and the per-session frozen
  injection blocks are untouched.

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
- **Settings → Engram Memory** — a standalone first-class settings section
  (right after the Plugins section, not a child tab of it). Default
  "All workspaces" view shows every workspace's memories/tasks/links
  grouped by workspace (dropdown + prev/next workspace pager; the memory
  table additionally pages 10 rows per page with a jump dropdown, fixed
  column widths, 3-line clamped content ellipsis and full text on hover).
  Overview
  stat cards (counts by workspace/kind, auto-capture totals, per-workspace
  `[ENGRAM]` index token estimate, cumulative GC totals), a searchable /
  filterable memory table with archive + delete actions, an ESR task board
  with an inline "new task" form and a per-task "fill evidence to close"
  (artifact / evaluation / memory_ref → STABLE, same gates as esr_close),
  a node + relation list (nodes are domain objects the model registers via
  esr_node — package/service/repo/concept; relations via esr_link), a separate
  **relation-graph** tab (hand-rolled force-directed SVG, no chart library so
  the bundle stays pure: entities as circles, tasks as check badges, relations
  colored per type with direction arrows; drag nodes, pan, wheel-zoom, re-lay

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
**Real behaviour telemetry (agent observability)** — the ESR page opens
  with an "agent behaviour" panel fed by a new `usage` table (per workspace
  × day rollup) + `GET /api/dsh-engram/stats`: every `engram_*`/`esr_*` tool call
  is recorded (counts, failures, recall mechanics). Reported ratios:
  **ESR proactivity** = esr calls / (memory + esr calls); **recall hit rate**
  = recalls returning ≥1 hit / total recalls; **mean hits per query**;
  **detail conversion** = a engram_detail following a hit recall within 8
  session events. Per-tool counts + a 14-day daily rollup are shown too.
  Numbers are real, from real sessions — lift ESR proactivity by watching
  this panel and tuning the injected prompt.
- **Settings → Engram Memory → 设置 tab** — the config card, expanded by default
  (DSH 0.2.1 dropped the `settings.plugin.item` slot, so the old
  Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration seat no longer renders). Same card,
  same transport: title + one-line description + chevron, its ~12 options under
  four groups — Capture & Search / Index / Lifecycle & GC / Security. Changes
  apply to new sessions (frozen blocks stay stable); Discard / Save with an
  "unsaved" badge on the hea

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
The browser half is served by DSH's client-module loader directly from this
package (`dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]`, no web-application rebuild); the
data comes from the loopback-fenced `/api/dsh-engram/*` route family. The fence
stays closed by default; to reach the memory viewer from an authorized tunnel
hostname, list it in the plugin's `trustedHosts` config (e.g. via the registry
or a profile patch):

readme.section: What you get in the GUI
readme.text:
```jsonc
// patch/engram.json
{ "engram": { "trustedHosts": ["cream-club-fragrances-caught.trycloudflare.com"] } }
```

If you change `client/src`, rebuild the bundle with:

```sh
npm run build:client
```

| Tool | Purpose | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `engram_store` | Explicitly store one memory (kind, tags, optional entity anchor, optional supersedes/contradicts ids, optional `source`/`conditions`) | write |
| `engram_recall` | Deterministic keyword recall over workspace memories; optional `search_sessions` FTS over past sessions; opt-in `scope=global`/`recallScope` cross-workspace recall with `[W:<ws>]` origin markers | read |
| `engram_detail` | Full record of one memory id (provenance, tags, hits) | read |
| `esr_task` | Create a task entity (draft → active) | write |
| `esr_close` | Close a task via the evidence protocol (artifact + evaluation + memory_ref) | write |
| `esr_link` | Add a typed relation between two entities (mini graph) | write |
| `esr_dep` | Add a dependency edge (blocks / relates-to / parent-of) between tasks | write |
| `esr_claim` | Atomically claim a task (assignee + claimedAt, draft → active) | write |
| `esr_unclaim` | Release a claimed task's assignee | write |
| `esr_ready` | List claimable tasks (no open blocker, unclaimed) | read |
| `esr_status` | Pull live ESR state + derived hints (`since_revision` short "unchanged" response) | read |
| `esr_node` | Cr

The `[ESR]` block is a frozen per-session snapshot and never auto-refreshes —
call `esr_status` for the live truth.

A scheduled sweep (`gcIntervalHours`, default 24h) plus a manual `esr_gc` /
GUI button keeps the store bounded the pi-esr way — **mechanical, working-set
protected, archive-only**:

GC never touches the working set: memories referenced by an active task
(`memory_refs`), task-kind memories, and already-indexed hits
(`hits >= promoteHits`). Run `esr_gc` with `dry_run: true` to preview. Nothing
is hard-deleted — the report ends with re-fetch pointers for everything it
archived, so archives are recoverable, not lost.

DSH's default context compression is a **lossy LLM full summary**
(`compaction-basic`): evicted history is crushed into prose — un-queryable, and
the summary itself burns tokens. dsh-engram's auto-GC replaces it:
`ContextGcEngine extends BasicCompactionEngine` overrides the single
`summarize()` hook and swaps the summary body for:

1. **Scan** — the evicted messages are scanned for provenance anchors: memory
   ids echoed by `engram_store`/`engram_recall`/`engram_detail`, `tsk_*`/`ent_*`
   touched by `esr_*`, and `file_path` anchors (`esr_gc` and other management
   calls are NOT anchors);
2. **Pointer summary** — every evicted category carries an explicit re-fetch
   call (`engram_detail(id: "…")` / `engram_recall(query)` / the [ESR] block /
   `esr_ready`); the active working set is restated, never evicted;
3. **Narrative safety net** — only un-provenanced turns (pure chat / reasoning)
   get a scoped LLM summary (`gcNarrative`, default on; off = the whole path is
   zero-LLM and un-provenanced turns are kept as truncated verbatim).

Triggers follow DSH's own compaction timing (step pressure / context-overflow /
`/compact`); the lock, replay validation, tool-call/result pairing and token
pricing are all reused from the basic engine. Any error falls back to the
default compressor — compaction is never broken; with `gcReplacesCompaction:
false` (the default since v0.6, or a host without `dsh-compaction-basic`) a bare
`BasicCompactionEngine` is mounted instead, so the `compaction` service never
disappears while dsh-engram is installed. Mounting registers the `compaction`
service on the plugin's fiber, so unloading/reloading engram restores the
default engine. **Taking over compaction is opt-in**: turn on
`gcReplacesCompaction` (and `autoWebCompaction` for web presets).

> **Shrink gate**: the harness refuses any checkpoint that is not strictly
> smaller than the evicted span (`summary is not smaller than the shadowed
> content`) and rolls the compaction back — otherwise the context never shrinks
> and the session eventually hits the model-side overflow. Context GC
> self-predicts that gate: it mirrors the harness framing with the host
> `tokenMeter` (verified token-for-token identical) and truncates the
> pointer/narrative body to the evicted span's token budget (the pointer head
> and working set survive; the trimmed tail stays recoverable in the session
> log), so compactions actually commit. Full from-scratch usage:
> [`docs/CONTEXT-GC-GUIDE.zh.md`](docs/CONTEXT-GC-GUIDE.zh.md).

readme.section: Where it is enabled (the entry point)
readme.text:
Assembly happens on **two planes**, but both switches are opt-in (no takeover by
default):

readme.section: Where it is enabled (the entry point)
readme.text:
- **Host plane (headless / TUI / base profiles)**:
  the main plugin (`lib/index.js`) mounts the engine inside `ctx.effect` via
  `mountCompactionEngine(ctx, resolved, { readWorkspace }) → new Engine()`,
  registering the `compaction` service on its own fiber; the plugin patch
  disables the base `compaction-basic` row, making engram the sole host-plane
  provider. `gcReplacesCompaction: false` (default) → a bare
  `BasicCompactionEngine` (DSH's own summarizer); `true` → `ContextGcEngine`
  (pointer summaries). Enable via profile patch
  (`config: { gcReplacesCompaction: true }`) or the settings card.
- **Preset plane (web profile) — covers every stock preset once enabled**: web keeps compaction inside each agent preset's isolated realm
  (the shipped presets mount their own `compaction-basic`), unreachable from a
  host-plane row — and unreachable from a profile patch too (`mountPreset`
  builds its `Include.Config` with no patches; verified against the harness
  source). So on boot, once the `agentPresets` service is ready, the plugin
  **auto-edits every preset that still has the stock layout** — the default
  preset plus the whole roster, across BOTH preset generations: legacy

readme.section: First impressions after an npm install (perceive / guide / configure)
readme.text:
- **Semi-automatic (opt-in)**: DSH's own summarizer stays the default. Turn on
  `gcReplacesCompaction` (host plane) and `autoWebCompaction` (web presets) in
  the settings card, then boot once — `mountCompactionEngine` takes over and
  the stock presets are rewritten. **No file editing after that.**
- **Perceivable**: at boot the plugin writes an authoritative snapshot to
  `$DSH_HOME/engram/context-gc.status.json` (`host` plane mode + the per-preset
  `web` results + effective config). At any time run `npx dsh-engram status` or
  `npx dsh-engram doctor`; the web memory board (ESR kanban) also shows a
  header chip ("Context GC·主机 ·N 预设") fed by the overview API. Two startup
  log lines confirm it too: `engram context-gc: compaction = Context GC …` and
  `engram web-provision: wired Context GC into preset …`.
- **Configurable**: one settings card (memory-GC section) governs everything:
  `autoWebCompaction` (web auto-wiring, default off), `gcReplacesCompaction`
  (Context GC vs host summarizer, default off), `gcNarrative` (narrative
  safety net).
  Changes take effect after restarting `dsh web`, and the web rows are
  refreshed to match automatically.

readme.section: First impressions after an npm install (perceive / guide / configure)
readme.text:
**Verify it took**: after restarting `dsh web` (or the profile) —
- host plane (headless/TUI/base): the startup log shows
`engram context-gc: compaction = Context GC (mechanical eviction + re-fetch pointers)`;
- web plane: the log shows one line per wired preset —
`engram web-provision: wired Context GC into preset "standard" (…); restart dsh web so sessions pick it up`,
or `npx dsh-engram status` reports `wired` for each; sessions composed
from ANY preset then compact via mechanical eviction + re-fetch pointers.
A line like `… keeping the existing compaction service` means another provider
already owns `compaction` in that realm (the swap didn't take); `web-provision … skipped (custom)`
means that preset was customized (or has no compaction group) and was left untouched;
`dsh-compaction-basic unavailable` means the backend is missing and everything
falls back to the default compressor.

readme.section: BoundaryPrune (subtask-boundary pruning, opt-in since v0.7.11 + ledger veto)
readme.text:
Context GC owns *what a compaction summary says*; BoundaryPrune owns *when a
deterministic prune fires*: at todo-completion progress and goal terminal
events, it calls DSH's own `toolResultPruner` (deterministic surface-replace,
zero LLM) so long-stale over-threshold tool results stop replaying in every
later request. The two switches are independent.

readme.section: BoundaryPrune (subtask-boundary pruning, opt-in since v0.7.11 + ledger veto)
readme.text:
- **Evidence chain** ([oracle analysis](docs/ORACLE-ANALYSIS.zh.md) +
  [proposal](docs/PROPOSAL-resultpack.zh.md)): 97 real sessions measured —
  2.77B–7.53B chars of tool-result replay exposure (~692M–1.88M tokens), 96%
  of result bytes from bash/read/run_code; the counterfactual simulation says
  todo boundaries cover 79% of that exposure and a repayment gate lifts
  cache-aware net savings 12–32% on every threshold config.
- **Repayment gate**: a prune rewrites the prefix (one KV-cache break), so it
  fires only while the session is still expected to run at least
  `boundaryPruneMinRemaining` (default 50) more requests — expectation is a
  workspace-history prior with ×2 growth projection past it, so long sessions
  are never starved.
- **Honest activation surface**: sessions with no goal and no todo progress
  simply never trigger (no boundary → no prune, zero side effects); the
  corpus-wide dry run activates on 38% of sessions. If the pruner service is
  absent the mechanism disables itself with one log line.
- **Live read (2026-10-26, two days of real use)**: the Context Ledger recorded
  the host pruning 64,200 chars on its own across two sessions (4 prunes in a
  220-req

BoundaryPrune makes pruning lossless: the removed middle of every pruned
tool result is redacted (same rules as the memory write path) and archived to
`~/.dsh/engram/resultpack/<callId>.json`, and the pruned surface node gets a
tail handle — `[middle archived: result_recall(<callId>) 可取]` — so the model
knows the full result is one step away. `result_recall(callId, offset?)`
returns the archived middle in paged text blocks (progressive disclosure, the
same philosophy as `[ENGRAM]` → `engram_detail`, and the complete
ObservationPack pattern from SoL-Pi mechanism ③).

- **Lossless by construction**: L1 pruning shrinks the replay; L2 keeps the
  original recoverable on demand — the "model rereads a pruned result" failure
  mode goes to zero.
- **Scoped cost**: archives live outside the memory domain (big blobs never
  bloat the domain JSON or the [ENGRAM] index); retention is a mtime sweep
  (`resultPackRetentionDays`, default 7) riding the same GC cadence.
- **Self-disabling**: L2 without `boundaryPrune` has nothing to archive, so it
  registers no tool and emits one warning.
- Default **off**: `resultPack: false` (must be on together with
  `boundaryPrune: true`). When active the log shows
  `engram result-pack enabled: result_recall(callId, offset) registered`.

Mechanisms must be provably activating, and dormant ones are off by default.
`/api/dsh-engram/stats` (and the GUI overview) now answer
`activation: { boundaryPrune, recall }`:

- `boundaryPrune` — cumulative, durable record of real BoundaryPrune fires
  (fires / prunedResults / charsRemoved / byKind todo|goal|step / lastFire),
  written to `~/.dsh/engram/boundary-prune.status.json` on every landed prune,
  independent of `resultPack`.
- `recall` — the injection leg of the recall funnel: how many `[RECALL]`
  blocks actually made it into sessions (`recall-injections.json`), closing
  the loop already measured from session logs (engram_recall queries → hits →
  engram_detail follows) so you can see injection→query→detail activation.

Turns "saves tokens" into a checkable number. Every model request is one ledger
tick: injected `[ENGRAM]`/`[RECALL]` and `[ESR]` blocks are charged per request
they survive; results removed by BoundaryPrune are credited per later request
they no longer replay; every prune pays one prefix-rewrite penalty
`(1 − ledgerCacheDiscount)` (the KV-cache break). `GET /api/dsh-engram/stats`
and `/overview` return `ledger`:

- `totals` — `requests / injectedChars / avoidedChars / rewriteCount /
  rewriteChars / netChars / netTokens` with
  `net = avoided − injected − rewriteChars × (1 − discount)`;
- `byWorkspace` / `byDay` — the same arithmetic per workspace and calendar day
  (`byDay` newest first);
- `openSessions` — sessions still accumulating in memory (a restart loses at
  most `flushEvery` requests).

The Telemetry tab renders it directly (net-token headline, saved / injected /
rewrite-penalty cards, a 14-day red/green net chart), and the memory overview
adds a "net context tokens" stat card. Durable rollup at
`~/.dsh/engram/ledger.json` (atomic write, daily buckets, delta flush); the hot
path is an integer add, zero I/O and zero model calls.
Defaults: `ledgerEnabled: true`, `ledgerCacheDiscount: 0.1`; off = no listeners,
no writes.

**Two credit legs** (v0.7.1 — before this the ledger only charged costs, so the
net was structurally negative):

1. **L1 boundary prune** — chars removed by `toolResultPruner`, credited per
   later request. Requires a host-plane `toolResultPruner`; DSH ≥ 0.2.0 web
   profiles move that row into each agent preset's isolate realm, so the bundle
   patch re-enables the host row — check `boundaryPrune.armed` in the status
   snapshot.
2. **Compaction (Context GC)** — every checkpoint credits `span chars −
   checkpoint chars` from the engine that produced it; host plane and the web
   preset realm (bridged through the `engramLedger` service) write the same
   ledger.

**Honest scope**: tokens are `chars / 4` estimates, not provider billing, and no
quality delta is claimed. Until a workspace actually prunes or compacts its
"saved" leg is 0, so the net equals injected + rewrite penalty (negative is
expected) — the Telemetry tab says so inline.

Pull-only recall measured dormant (24 `engram_recall` / 8 `engram_detail` across
112 real sessions), so v0.6 pushes on three deterministic events instead. One
line per event, at most 3 lines per session (`jitMaxLines`, `jitMaxLineChars`=220),
and silence when there is nothing relevant to point at:

| Event | Trigger | What is pushed |
|---|---|---|
| Error recurrence | the same `cmd:` signature fails a second time and a prior error/procedure memory exists | that memory's id + a one-line excerpt + `engram_detail` |
| File focus | the same file is edited twice in a row and a filePath/dir-anchored memory exists | preference first, then fact/decision |
| Goal completion | goal complete/block while active ESR tasks remain | the first two open tasks + `esr_status` |

- **Append-only**: a pushed line is never edited or withdrawn, so the prefix
  changes once per push. Each push charges a rewrite
  (`estimatePrefixChars + line length`) in the Context Ledger
  (`rewriteCount` / `rewriteChars`), visible on the telemetry page.
- **Silent without a hit** — no memory/task to point at, no line.
- **Zero LLM, pure rules**; `jitEnabled:false` disables it, and the empty
  `[JIT]` section costs nothing.
- **Not yet**: the resume brief (next-day continuation) and an explicit
  remaining-requests ROI gate — today the 3-line budget plus the ledger are the
  guardrails.

- **episode** — at `session/disposed`, a zero-LLM digest of the event log: files
  touched, commands run, failures that later recovered (`cmd×N→fixed`), written
  commit subjects, and still-open todos. Written only when there is substance (a
  bare `ls` session produces none); **never indexed**; the newest 20 per
  workspace are kept and older ones archived.
- **resume brief** — at the first assembly of a new session, the newest episode
  from the last 7 days is injected as a `[RESUME]` line (≤240 chars) plus an
  `engram_detail <id>` pointer, frozen with `[ENGRAM]`/`[RECALL]`. No recent
  episode → no line; returning to a project does not need a re-briefing.
- Settings: `episodeEnabled`, `resumeBriefEnabled` (both default on), plus
  `episodeMaxPerWorkspace` / `resumeBriefMaxAgeDays` / `resumeBriefMaxChars`.

> **Host requirement (silent-dormancy warning).** Episode, resume brief, `[RECALL]`
> and the session-end todo sink all read the session's event log. On ≥0.2.x hosts
> the log arrives through `ctx.sessionQuery.live()`, `session.snapshotEvents()` or,
> as a last resort, `session.seq` + `session.eventAt(seq)`. A host that exposes
> **none** of these keeps the three features dormant: memory storage, `engram_recall`
> and `engram_detail` still work, but nothing is injected at session start and no
> episode is written. The plugin logs one `engram: this host exposes no readable
> session event log … Session surface: …` warning per session naming what the
> session object does offer — that line is the thing to paste into a bug report.
> Known case: the **desktop runtime** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-runtime`) on
> Windows, tracked as issue #9.
>
> `dsh-engram status` also prints a **push-legs** line — `推送腿：事件日志读法
> sessionQuery · 最近 …` — the read path the live process actually took, written
> to `$DSH_HOME/engram/push-legs.jsonl`. A dormant host shows
> `事件日志不可读（none）… 休眠中` there, so the four features can be checked
> without hunting a startup log.

`esr_node` grows from a dot on the graph into a readable **page**: current
truth, timeline, open loops, conflicts and relations for one thing
(package / repo / service / bug…).

- **Entity card (in the index, default on)** — `[ENGRAM]` renders ONE line for
  each active entity (anchored memories or open tasks), at most 2:
  `[ENT] dsh-engram · package · 3 mem · 1 open · truth: … #id · page: engram_detail(entity="dsh-engram")`
  Those entities' flat memory lines are not repeated; other entities stay in a
  single `nodes:` line.
- **Full page (on drill)** — `engram_detail(entity="<name|id>")` returns
  `truth / timeline / open loops / conflicts / relations`, with memory ids and
  evidence gaps. A name with anchored memories but no registered node still
  gets a virtual page.
- Pure, deterministic: preference leads `truth`, superseded rows never enter
  it, conflicts are de-duplicated by unordered pair (`#a vs #b`).
- Settings `entityCardsEnabled` (default on); `entityCardsMax` /
  `entityCardChars` tunable.

"Treating the past as truth" is the strongest credibility critique against
memory plugins. v0.7 gives file-backed memories an **anchor**:

- on write, record `{path, mtimeMs, size, hash?}` (sha256 for files ≤256KB,
  stat only for larger ones) in the memory row; relative paths resolve against
  the workspace;
- at session start a bounded revalidation (≤40 rows) tags changed/missing
  sources `stale`; the `[ENGRAM]` index and entity `truth` stop showing them,
  but nothing is deleted — `engram_detail` still returns them and the entity
  timeline marks `· stale`;
- **layered TTL**: `preference` / `procedure` permanent; `episode` 14 days;
  `error` 60 days; everything else `expireDays` (180). Hard deletes still do not
  exist — GC only archives.
- Settings: `anchorRevalidate` (default on), `episodeTtlDays`, `errorTtlDays`.
- **Not done**: the offline consolidation job (episode abstraction/merge) —
  deterministic rules can only roll up, not abstract semantically; deferred
  until v0.8 alongside playbooks, rather than shipping a lossy pseudo-merge.

Capture is deterministic and offline — it only sees tool *results*, never the
conversation. Exactly what earns a memory record:

| Tool result | Action | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `git commit … -m "subject"` | record — the written subject is the memory | 0.55 |
| `git merge` / `rebase` / `cherry-pick` / `tag` / `checkout -b` | record (milestone) | 0.5 |
| `git push` / `git stash` / commit without `-m` | **skip** — plumbing echo, not a decision | — |
| write/edit of a significant config & doc path | record | 0.3 |
| read of a config path | record | 0.3 |
| repeated tool error | record (deduped by message) | 0.25 |

Explicit `engram_store` writes are always recorded regardless of these rules
(rate-limited per session).

**Who earns a `[ENGRAM]` index line** (this is what actually touches the prompt):
`signal >= minIndexSignal` **or** `hits >= promoteHits` **or** `kind === "task"`,
then capped by `indexMaxLines` / `indexMaxChars`.

**Procedures are evidence-gated (v0.8-A).** An auto-captured `fixed: <cmd>` row is
a hypothesis, not a lesson: it starts with `evidenceCount = 1` and stays out of
the index until the same command is verified **3** times with the last
verification younger than **14 days** (`procedureMinEvidence` /
`procedureMaxAgeDays`). The moment that command fails again the row is
invalidated (`invalidatedBy` = the failing memory's id, signal → 0.2) and leaves
the index immediately — a just-broken procedure is worse than none, because the
next agent would copy it verbatim. Hand-written procedures with no evidence
fields keep the older `hits >= promoteHits` path.

**Promoted procedures can become real Skills (v0.8-B).** An index line is a
hint; a DSH Skill is an artifact the host discovers, advertises in the session
catalog, and any agent (or subagent) can load in full:

```bash
npx dsh-engram skill export            # → <workspace>/.dsh/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
npx dsh-engram skill export --dry-run  # show the plan, touch nothing
```

Only procedures that pass the evidence gate are exported (`≥3` verified
successes, verified within 14 days, not invalidated). Each file carries a
`generated-by` marker: the exporter rewrites and eventually **deletes** only its
own files, so a hand-written skill sharing the root is never touched. When a
procedure stops holding, its skill file disappears on the next export — the host
catalog must not keep advertising a fix that just broke. `npm run skill:check`
proves the seam end-to-end by loading DSH's own `dsh-skill-filesystem` provider
and listing the exported skill through it.

**The approval queue is in the GUI too (v0.8.4).** The memory tab shows
"Playbook 待批准" with evidence counts and approve/revoke buttons, backed by
`GET|POST /api/dsh-engram/approvals`. The route recomputes the list with the same
planner `skill export` uses, so a click can never approve something the CLI would
skip; revoking returns a row to pending rather than deleting its evidence.

**Writing a skill needs a human yes (v0.8-D).** Evidence (`≥3` verified
successes) gets a procedure into the private index line; it does not, on its own,
put a file where the host advertises it to every agent. `skill export` therefore
writes only **approved** procedures — `skill pending` lists what is waiting,
`skill approve <id>` / `skill revoke <id>` maintain the record in
`~/.dsh/engram/playbook-approvals.json` (kept out of the memory store: an approval
is a human act, and a pool must not approve itself), and `--force` is the audited
escape hatch. Three successful runs prove a command worked; they do not prove the
instruction is sound.

**Subagent reports become durable capsules (v0.8-C, advisory).** A child's final
report above `capsuleMinSourceChars` (1500) is distilled by structure — headings,
bullets, question marks, next-step cues — into a `handoff` memory (结论 / 证据 /
未决 / 下一步) whose footer records `source → capsule` chars. It does **not** shrink
what the parent reads: DSH emits `tools/result` to observers only ("without
exposing a mutation or error channel into the outcome"), so substitution needs a
host seam that does not exist yet. What you get today is durability — the
conclusion survives the child session and compaction — plus a real measurement of
the saving for the day that seam lands. One extra guard keeps the pipe
clean: auto-captured git command echoes — text that embeds a shell chain
(`git push: cd … && …`) — stay out of the index even when above the signal
threshold, until recall hits have promoted them. Everything else sits quietly in
storage, reachable on demand via `engram_recall` / `engram_detail` — "retrieved ≠
injected".

What the model actually sees (rendered once per session, then frozen):

```
ESR operating protocol (static, byte-identical every turn)
  1. Before starting: esr_ready to see claimable work; esr_status for live state.
  2. Multi-step work → esr_task (draft first); claim → esr_claim; finish → esr_close (all three gates).
  state is the single source of truth: unsure → call esr_status.

[ENGRAM] workspace: symbolic-index · 2 memories · 1 task(s) active · 0 links
[D] 06-18 Decided: use sqlite-vec for retrieval #a2331d87
[T] 06-18 Retrieval upgrade — ACTIVE · gap: artifact, evaluation, memory_ref #tsk_8b26
drill: use [RECALL] below · engram_detail <id> (full record) · engram_recall <query> (more) · esr_task/esr_node/esr_link (work)

[RECALL] recall · 1 hit(s) · first msg: retrieval
- [D] 06-18 Decided: use sqlite-vec for retrieval upgrade #a2331d87 ×2
context: use above · engram_detail <id> · engram_recall <query>

[ESR] tasks: 1 active / 1 stable
- tsk_0d: Retrieval upgrade — ACTIVE · gap: artifact, evaluation, memory_ref
- closed: tsk_9a (RAG eval)  ·  +1
snapshot from session start — WILL NOT auto-refresh; call esr_status for live state

promote: 2 pending todo(s) vs 1 ESR task(s) — esr_task(name="…") #suggest-promote
```

Prefixes: `[D]` decision · `[E]` error · `[P]` procedure · `[F]` fact ·
`[I]` insight · `[H]` handoff · `[T]` task. A procedure re-used enough times
(`hits >= promoteHits`) becomes a "proven experience" — its prefix upgrades to
`[P✓]` and it is stably ranked first in the block (newest-first within each
group, keeping the block deterministic): our zero-LLM counterpart to TencentDB
Agent Memory's "Skill = validated, executable experience". Membership follows
the *Auto-capture policy* (signal threshold / recall promotion / git-echo guard),
bounded by the configured line and character budgets. `#` ids address the full
records via `engram_detail`. When a workspace has no tasks, `[ESR]` still renders
one line naming `esr_task`/`esr_close` so the mechanism stays visible to the
model instead of vanishing.

`[RECALL]` (session-start auto recall, `autoRecallOnStart`) runs one deterministic
BM25 pass over the workspace keyed on the session's first user message and injects
the top `autoRecallLimit` hits, bounded by the `autoRecallMaxChars` character
budget; nothing renders on zero hits or an empty workspace. It is a *pointer* — the
model should treat it as "this is relevant; `engram_detail` for the full record" —
rather than full-text dumping. It is a pure read (never bumps `hits`), superseded
stale truth never occupies a slot, and it freezes per session with `[ENGRAM]`.

Defaults are token-conscious; override any key via the profile patch
(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`) or the web config card:

```yaml
- id: engram
  config:
    autoCapture: true        # zero-LLM tool-result capture
    autoCapturePreferences: true  # zero-LLM user-correction/preference capture (prefer/avoid/switch-to cues)

```sh
npm test            # 381 tests: core + web API + GC + usage-observability + Context GC + ESR triggers + BoundaryPrune + preference learning + Context Ledger + JIT push (node:test)
npm run eval        # offline recall + structure benchmark (deterministic)
npm run build:client
```

readme.section: Testing & evaluation (two layers of real testing)
readme.text:
**npm run eval** (eval/recall-bench.mjs) is the deterministic layer —
LongMemEval-style: a controlled corpus (ASCII + CJK, known tags/entities/
timestamps) measured through the real store/recall path (openEngramDomain +
domain.recall), reporting Precision@k / Recall@k / MRR / Hit@1 per probe
(exact tag, substring, multi-term, CJK, phrase-single, ordering, negative)
plus StructMemEval-flavoured structure metrics (exact-duplicate dedup rate,
entity anchoring coverage, dangling-link hygiene). Honest, reproducible
numbers — everyone gets the same output. Current run: AVG P@k 0.770 /
AVG R@k 1.000 / MRR 0.889 / hit@1 0.889 / 0 negative false-positives /
dedup 1.0.

readme.section: Testing & evaluation (two layers of real testing)
readme.text:
**/api/dsh-engram/stats + the observability panel** is the real-session layer —
it answers how the model actually uses the memory in production (ESR
proactivity ratio, recall hit rate, detail conversion), while the eval
answers how good the retrieval layer itself is. The stats read the
concatenated multi-frame `session.jsonl.zstd` logs with Node's built-in
`node:zlib` (frame scan + one reused decoder handle) — **no system `zstd` CLI
is required**, so the telemetry works out-of-the-box on Windows and other
hosts without an external codec.

readme.section: Testing & evaluation (two layers of real testing)
readme.text:
Repo layout: `lib/` (host half: store / capture / index-block / tools / api /
settings), `client/` (browser half, TSX + `build.mjs`), `test/` (node:test).

**The web GUI opens and immediately shows “Failed to load plugins”**, with a
loader error like:

```
failed to apply loader entry … (@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings):
keyed slot "settings.plugin.item" requires options.key
```

Cause: DSH hosts since `0.1.0-rc.7` declare the config-card slot
`settings.plugin.item` as **keyed by the settings namespace a card edits** —
which is exactly how dsh-engram's own config card registers (under
`key: "dsh-engram"`). The `@linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all` family **before 0.2.0**
(`dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings`) registered its group card into that slot
**without a `key`**, and because a single failed loader entry aborts the whole
boot, the GUI stays stuck on the failure page.

Fixes:

- **Proper fix — upgrade the family**: `@linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all@^0.2.x`.
  The 0.2 line moved its settings surface out of the keyed slot into a
  first-level `settings.section` (the upstream fix for exactly this error).
- **Immediate unblock**: add `key: "web-ui-plugins"` to that one
  `settings.plugin.item` registration in the installed
  `node_modules/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings/lib/client.js`, then
  restart `dsh web`. (Under namespace-keyed dispatch the group card simply
  stays hidden; nothing else on the page is affected.)
